The 2027 Hopper Mini Is the Mini Squaredrop Trailer Ready for All Kinds of Adventures
15 photos
Photo: Modern Buggy RV
Summer might be the universal season for RV adventures, but fall is when the goodies drop. Each fall, manufacturers from all over the world showcase their new models and upgraded old ones, in preparation for the upcoming year and season.
U.S.-based Modern Buggy is among these manufactures. For the 2027 model year, Modern Buggy is expanding its two existing lines, the Modern Buggy and the Hopper series, refining existing floorplans and adding new ones that cover demands not met before. Highlights for the latter include the all-new Hopper 22 , the biggest of all Hoppers, and the Hopper Mini XL that we covered this week.
Also new but not as featured on the Modern Buggy social media pages is the Hopper Mini, which is the scaled-down version of the Mini XL, as its name clearly says. It seems that the manufacturer is planning on launching a new Mini Series within the Hopper lineup, designed with the same design language and focus on functionality, but more streamlined.
That makes the Hopper Mini your typical squaredrop trailer. Compared to the other Hoppers or even its bigger brother, the Mini XL , it's a mini squaredrop, but it can still offer sleeping up to four people, according to the official description.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV Chances are this is only possible by adding a rooftop tent, because in standard spec, as shown in photos in the gallery, the Mini only has sleeping for two inside, thanks to a fold-out mattress that does double duty as a lounge/sofa during the day and a bed at night.
The Hopper Mini is designed to compact, lightweight, durable, and affordable – ready to go whenever, wherever you might be thinking of taking it. It's perfectly capable of handling rougher terrains with its beefy tires and 14-inch (35.5-cm) ground clearance, and it will help you get off the grid for a little while, if that's your idea of fun, being prepped for solar.
Modern Buggy brought a pre-production unit of the Hopper Mini on display at a couple of recent trade events, where it accompanied its brother, the Mini XL. I couldn't find any videos from any one of these occasions, but some are bound to pop up as the unit goes into full production and makes its way to dealer lots.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV The full list of specs will also be finalized until then. For the time being, we know that this squaredrop is 12 feet 6 inches (3.8 meters) long, riding on a custom axle with a 2,200-lb (998-kg) single axle with torsion suspension, upgradable to Timbren independent suspension at an extra charge. Empty weight is at 1,195 lbs (542 kg), so it's towable by a wide range of vehicles.
The Hopper Mini is the essence of a basecamp, but built with typical Modern Buggy reliable, no-wood construction. On top of that custom chassis, you get a body with an aluminum frame and Azdel sidewalls, a one-piece Azdel-backed fiberglass roof, and framed slider windows. This trailer is made to last a lifetime even with extended use and exposure to the elements, and designed to cover the basics on wilder adventures.
Like the Hopper Mini XL, the Hopper Mini features a tailgate galley with a stainless steel sink, a solid surface countertop on which you can add whatever cooktop you already have, and a spot underneath for a 12V cooler or fridge. Storage is in netted open cubbies, both on considerations of costs and to reduce overall weight, but you do have plenty options.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV One of these cubbies is a pass-through that communicates with the interior, which will come in handy in bad weather. As for the interior, it matches the galley stylistically, which means more netted open cubbies and more fiberglass.
A foam mattress sofa is included in standard spec, as is a power vent that will help with ventilation with the opening windows. Photos show a smart TV mounted on the campside wall, and that's probably also standard because Modern Buggy doesn't mention it among the list of options.
That list includes a bigger battery to run house functions, the upgraded suspension, and a 5,000-BTU AC mounted in the rear wall at the expense of one of those storage compartments.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV Outside, the Hopper Mini come with a covered underbelly, a front rock guard, an aluminum luggage rack with a payload capacity in excess of 600 lbs (272 kg), an accessory hitch, and heavy-duty fenders with corner steps that can support up to 300 lbs (136 kg) of weight.
"The Hopper Mini is the perfect choice for outdoor enthusiasts looking for a light-weight, affordable, and easy-to-use option for their overland adventures," Modern Buggy says of the smallest of the Hoppers, adding that it's "designed for comfort with plenty of storage, dedicated sleeping space, and an outdoor kitchen with all the essentials."
Photo: Modern Buggy RV
The Hopper Mini is for those who prioritize adventure over creature comforts or home-like amenities, for adventurers who want a roof over their hand and basic facilities for everything else. It's not a complete solution and it doesn't claim to be.
Now, since the spec list isn't yet final, we don't have an MSRP for the Hopper Mini. Word online has it that it could be at $22,500, with sale prices ranging between $12,000 to $13,000.
